promises.value: Said he would "Lower real estate taxes and eliminate wasteful spending."
Said he would "Implement an environmental infrastructure reconstruction program focused on rebuilding our wastewater" systems.
Said he would "Streamline the county's Engineering, Public Works and Building departments to increase efficiency" and "speed permitting and cut departmental red tape."
Said he would "Implement a program of real estate tax credits to encourage affordable, market-based housing development."
"I will lead the charge to rebuild our environmental infrastructure."
"We should eliminate sales taxes on the cost of materials for housing, to help make housing more affordable."
On transit: "we should decrease and limit the use of large buses," shifting toward technology-based, point-to-point service.
On home rule: "Our cities must be allowed to develop or redevelop as determined by their residents, not by politicians in Tallahassee."
After the election, wrote on Facebook that "Pinellas County needs rebuilding now and I can't wait to roll up my sleeve and get the job done."
Did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 Candidate Connection survey.

electionHistory.value: 2024 general, County Commission District 1 (at-large): won. Chris Scherer (R) 262,740 (52.98%); Joanne 'Cookie' Kennedy (D) 233,197 (47.02%).
2024 Republican primary, District 1: canceled; Scherer advanced without appearing on the ballot.
Assumed office Nov 19, 2024; current term ends Nov 21, 2028.

keyPositions.value: Voted no on the $312.5 million Rays stadium bond resolution, which passed 5 to 2 on Dec 17, 2024. He had hoped to delay the vote again and said he might have gotten to yes eventually.
Before the Dec 17, 2024 bond vote, pushed for another delay, saying the commission should not vote on bonds until the Rays met all conditions.
On the Rays deal after his election (Nov 2024): "We are in a new era right here," adding that "whatever was agreed to before needs to be looked at differently now."

financialDisclosures.value: Form 6 for 2024, received 9/16/2025 (Commission on Ethics filer PID 312721)
Form 6 for 2025, received 9/3/2026 (Commission on Ethics filer PID 312721)

A separate filer record under the same name, John Christopher Scherer (PID 234524), shows Form 1 filings for 2012 to 2015 as a member of the St. Petersburg Development Review Commission (received 6/20/2013, 8/4/2014, 6/15/2015, 6/7/2016). The record does not confirm this is the same person.
A fines-accrued search for 2024 under the last name Scherer returned no records.

promises.value: "To bring common sense business decision making to the Pinellas County Commission. Less government is better government, lower taxes are better than higher taxes, and more freedom is better than less freedom."
Listed goals of lowering taxes, reducing regulations, "re-envisioning transit services delivery, and enacting term limits."
On housing: "Greater emphasis on down payment assistance," a county-owned land model for new multifamily rentals, and a faster, cheaper permitting process.

Priorities as summarized by the Times editorial board: "Lowering taxes, re-envisioning transit service and keeping the county affordable for everyone"; wants to "cut excess spending and wasteful programs."
Said he wants to bring "a conservative majority back to the Pinellas County Commission" and proposed smart grid technology to improve traffic signal timing.
Campaign site: "On the Pinellas County Commission, he will fight for the conservative values that make Pinellas great."
"Whatever happens in November, my approach is the same: keep cutting the property tax rate, as we have 4 of the last 5 years, saving taxpayers over $100 million, while fully funding public safety."
If property taxes are cut by the state, would "freeze open positions, and stress-test every department for 10 percent savings before ever touching essential services."
Said more than 30 types of building inspections would move online "by the end of 2026" and called for a countywide stormwater master plan.
On Tax Increment Financing commitments over $100 million: "So yes, I am open to voter approval for commitments of that scale."
Campaign site: "local government must adjust tax rates to prevent backdoor tax increases on homeowners"; supports beach renourishment, stormwater systems and flood protection.
Did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

electionHistory.value: 2022 Republican primary, County Commission District 2 (at-large): won. Brian Scott 57,798 (66.27%); Debbie Buschman 29,418 (33.73%).
2022 general, District 2: won, unseating the incumbent. Brian Scott 223,865 (53.99%); Patricia 'Pat' Gerard 190,779 (46.01%).
2026: Republican primary canceled; on the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot against Tim Hughes (D).
Assumed office Nov 22, 2022; current term ends Nov 17, 2026.

keyPositions.value: Voted yes on the Rays stadium bond resolution, Dec 17, 2024 (passed 5 to 2).
Elected 2025 commission chair on Nov 19, 2024.

As chair, the final FY 2026 budget set the general fund rate at 4.5423 mills, which the county called its lowest level since 1990; Scott said: "I'm proud of the work the Commission accomplished in concert with County staff."
At an Aug 14, 2025 workshop after a state DOGE visit, said Commissioner Nowicki should make specific requests for each department rather than requesting information for the entire county.
Served on the Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority board from 2012 to 2018, before his election.

promises.value: Announcing his run: "I am a conservative outsider who has seen what liberal policies can do to a city."
"I will not allow Pinellas County to become like St. Petersburg, filled with crime and over development."
Campaign site promoted term limits: "Advocating for term limits to prevent career politicians from dominating"; also listed sewage releases, taxes and infrastructure spending as issues.
Campaign site: "We need someone who is not afraid to challenge the status quo and the entrenched bureaucrats and fight for the people."
Declined to answer all questions in the League of Women Voters guide for the Aug 2024 elections.

electionHistory.value: 2024 general, County Commission District 3 (at-large): won, unseating the incumbent. Vince Nowicki (R) 253,412 (51.31%); Charlie Justice (D) 240,458 (48.69%).
2024 Republican primary, District 3: canceled; David Leatherwood (R) withdrew or was disqualified.
2021: ran for St. Petersburg mayor but withdrew before the qualifying deadline.
Assumed office Nov 19, 2024; current term ends Nov 21, 2028.

keyPositions.value: Voted no on the Rays stadium bond resolution, Dec 17, 2024 (passed 5 to 2).

At a Nov 25, 2024 Tiger Bay forum: "I look forward to bringing up a special election to leave it up to the voters countywide" on the Rays deal; also said "let's make sure we're investing in our water and sewer first."

At an Aug 14, 2025 workshop, said he would support eliminating certain staff positions if the "same analysis is applied to all county employees," and asked for reports on staff phone and email volume.

Voted yes on Dec 16 (2025) to build a 2,000-space airport parking garage while objecting to its location: "I'm supportive because I think that's the will of the board, but I just really can't get a clear answer on why we are not building in the short-term lot first."

Form 6 for 2025, received 6/30/2026 (Commission on Ethics filer PID 312717)

conflicts.value: In a Feb 2026 letter, County Administrator Barry Burton wrote that Nowicki met with Allegiant Air without informing him or other commissioners, calling it "unprofessional" and a violation of the county charter. Nowicki responded: "A lot of the facts in the letter are wrong."

Said at an Aug 14, 2025 workshop that he sought an ethics opinion before considering the Treasure Island interim city manager role and chose not to apply: "my full focus is on serving Pinellas County."

promises.value: Supported the Greenlight Pinellas transit tax during his first county campaign; cited "My fiscally responsible approach to governing Dunedin."
"Sitting on the BOCC and Tampa Bay Water Board allows me to address as a priority water and affordability issues."

Top funding priorities: "invest in public safety (Sheriff and all first responder departments), continue to invest in our infrastructure replacement and improvement (water, sewer, roads, bridges resiliency)" and economic development for higher paying jobs.
Campaign site: "Dave Eggers is leading the fight on the County Commission to roll back the millage rate"; pledged to "fight for a more responsive building department."
After the primary, said he is "committed to defending our conservative values on the Pinellas County Commission."
Told the Times editorial board he was likely to support lowering the tax rate in the upcoming budget.
Would focus on attracting target industries that offer higher-paying jobs if elected to a third term (paraphrase by reporter).
Campaign site priorities: "STORM RECOVERY", "TACKLING WASTE, FRAUD AND ABUSE", "BRINGING DOWN PROPERTY TAXES", "SUPPORTING VETERANS AND SENIORS", beach renourishment, "STANDING WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT".
Campaign emphasized spending on utility systems, supporting public safety and attracting employers with higher-paying jobs (paraphrase by reporter).
Did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

electionHistory.value: 2014 general, County Commission District 4 (open seat): won. Preliminary results: Dave Eggers (R) 53,011 (60.87%); Mark Weinkrantz (D) 28,749 (33.01%); Marcus Harrison (NPA) 3,171 (3.64%); Carl Folkman (NPA) 2,152 (2.47%). Certified 2014 results were not found on the SOE site.
2014: emerged from a seven-candidate Republican primary for District 4 (vote totals not found).
2018: won District 4 without appearing on the ballot.
2022 primary, District 4 (universal primary, open to all voters): won. Dave Eggers 35,886 (67.74%); Heather Aynne Vernillo 17,089 (32.26%). No general election contest followed.
2026 Republican primary, District 4: won. Dave Eggers 35,071 (78.51%); Anthony Ringelspaugh 9,600 (21.49%).
2026 general election for District 4 canceled; Eggers won without appearing on the Nov 3 ballot.
Candidate-supplied bio: Dunedin City Commission 2003 to 2009; Dunedin Mayor 2009 to 2014; County Commissioner 2014 to present.

keyPositions.value: Voted against the Rays stadium deal in July 2024, then voted yes on the bond resolution Dec 17, 2024: commissioners "made a commitment back in July to the deal that is on the table, and I think there's something to be said for us making commitments."
Opposed the commission's April 2022 vote to sue the state over an election law (SB 524) that put single-member seats on the 2022 ballot.

Pushed the commission to place a referendum limiting commissioners to three terms or 12 years; the motion failed with Kathleen Peters as its only other supporter (reported in a 2022 article as having happened the year before).
As 2026 chair, on Nowicki's contact with Allegiant: "when you start talking on behalf of the commission, and you start talking against what the commission has voted for, it becomes a problem."
The Times editorial board wrote that he supported rolling back the property tax rate for the then-current budget.

electionHistory.value: 2014 Republican primary, Florida House District 67: won. Christopher Latvala 6,108 (67.2%); Christopher Shepard 2,985 (32.8%).
2014 general, House District 67: defeated Steve Sarnoff (D) with 53%.
2016 general, House District 67: won. Latvala 40,587 (58.57%); David S. Vogel (D) 28,711 (41.43%).
2018 general, House District 67: won. Latvala 33,600 (54.0%); Dawn Douglas (D) 28,672 (46.0%).
2020 general, House District 67: won. Latvala 47,018 (57.0%); Dawn Douglas (D) 35,457 (43.0%).
2022, County Commission District 5: won without opposition; general election canceled.

Context for 2022: a state election law (SB 524) required single-member commission seats, including District 5, to be on the 2022 ballot. Latvala had filed in 2021 to run for the seat in 2024; commissioners referred to the bill as aiding him, and he pushed back on those allegations.
2024, District 5: won re-election without appearing on the ballot; term ends Nov 21, 2028.

keyPositions.value: Voted against the Rays stadium deal in July 2024, then voted yes on the bond resolution Dec 17, 2024: "I hope our vote today helps set the wheels in motion for a new owner and a new era of Tampa Bay Rays baseball."
In April 2025 proposed an elected county mayor; after a May 15, 2025 workshop he backed away and suggested "Maybe we look at having a chair have a two-year term."
At an Aug 14, 2025 workshop, criticized Commissioner Nowicki over the Treasure Island city manager role while saying scrutinizing county positions is Nowicki's job.
In 2021, as chair of the House Education and Employment Committee, supported legislation to bar transgender athletes from high school girls' sports.
Ballotpedia's BillTrack50 list of bills he sponsored includes HB 1557 Parental Rights in Education (2022) and HB 7 Individual Freedom (2022), both later chaptered into law.

promises.value: Campaigned on education reform in the 2012 House primary.
Congressional campaign theme: "If families and businesses have to live within their means, then so should our government."
Congressional campaign theme on flood insurance, citing "over 50,000 homeowners and 1,500 small businesses in Pinellas County" affected.
Planned to keep working on mental health as a commissioner and to create a program giving people detained under the Marchman Act "beds and substance abuse counseling programs" (reporter's account).

Campaign site: "She also opposes the proposed increased gas tax in Pinellas."

electionHistory.value: 2012 Republican primary, Florida House District 69: won. Kathleen Peters 6,662 (51%); David Phillips 4,756 (36.4%); Jim Dobyns 1,643 (12.6%).
2012 general, House District 69: won. Peters 40,164 (52.3%); Josh Shulman (D) 36,577 (47.7%).
Jan 14, 2014 special Republican primary, U.S. House District 13: lost. David Jolly 20,337 (44.6%); Peters 14,120 (31%); Mark Bircher 11,158 (24.5%). Unofficial AP results.
2014 general, House District 69: defeated Scott T. Orsini (D); unopposed in the primary. Vote totals not listed.
2016 general, House District 69: won. Peters 47,882 (56.55%); Jennifer Webb (D) 36,791 (43.45%).
2018 Republican primary, County Commission District 6: won. Kathleen Peters 12,034 (47.93%); Larry Ahern 8,937 (35.59%); Barb Haselden 4,137 (16.48%).
2018 general, District 6: won. Kathleen Peters 66,963 (60.24%); Amy Kedron (D) 44,203 (39.76%).
2022: won District 6 without appearing on the ballot.
2026: Republican primary canceled; on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot against David Glenn Jr. (D). Term ends Nov 17, 2026.
Elected to the South Pasadena City Commission in 2008; selected mayor in 2009; served until 2012.

keyPositions.value: Voted yes on the Rays stadium bond resolution Dec 17, 2024: "Today we made a decision to let the world know that we're still great collaborative partners."
Opposed the commission's April 2022 vote to sue the state over SB 524.
Was the only other commissioner to support Eggers' motion for a term-limits referendum (three terms or 12 years), which failed.
As 2024 chair, made committee assignments that removed Commissioner Flowers from the PSTA board; the board approved them 6 to 1. Peters said the move was not personal.
In May 2025 opposed creating an elected county mayor, citing the difficulty of removing a corrupt elected mayor.
Says property tax rate cuts in four of the last five years returned more than $100 million to taxpayers (candidate's statement).
Campaign site states she "was the only Pinellas County Commissioner to oppose raising taxes on residents in 2021" (candidate's claim; vote record not independently checked).
As a state representative, sponsored HB 1137 (Pinellas County Construction Licensing Board), which became Chapter 2018-179.

"I will continue into the next term with focus and without disruption" (from her Florida Public Media voter guide survey); declined an interview.

promises.value: Would form a task force with county and city staff on flood risk, with the goal of working with the insurance industry to "reduce property insurance rates."
Proposes converting old mobile home parks into affordable condominium parks, with low-income mobile home owners eligible to buy a unit.
Would form a regional transportation task force including "electric bus lines, a regional subway system, and inner-city trolley systems."
"I oppose high-density building in high-hazard flood zones" that does not meet real resilience standards.
Would "establish an inter-governmental resiliency task force, fund a countywide GIS mapping every stormwater and drainage system."
On Tax Increment Financing over $100 million going to voters: "Yes, at a commitment of that size."
Would "pursue Penny for Pinellas and a TDT change to fund regional light rail."

electionHistory.value: 2026: Democratic primary canceled; on the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot for County Commission District 2 against incumbent Brian Scott (R). No earlier races found.

promises.value: Plans to hold "Workdays," doing jobs around the county to connect with workers (reporter's summary of his answer).

Would raise county revenue without raising taxes through "increased vertical land development initiatives in carefully selected areas" and tourism, reinvesting in "public transit, parks & recreation, library services."
"eliminating property taxes is not a viable option."
"we need to build more vertically in certain locations rather than out horizontally."
On Tax Increment Financing referendums: "Let the elected leaders make the hard decisions."
"We also need to continue the planning for a commuter rail network in Pinellas County."

electionHistory.value: 2026: Democratic primary canceled; on the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot for County Commission District 6 against incumbent Kathleen Peters (R). No earlier races found.

promises.value: "I believe the person that sits in the seat should represent everyone in Pinellas, not just one district."
On teachers: "teachers are really tired of performative listening"; wants to listen to, empower and pay them.
"I will advocate for competitive teacher pay, support referendums that fund compensation, and reduce unnecessary burdens."
"I will be an unapologetic advocate for a strong and well-funded public school system." "Voucher programs should have reasonable income limits and include transparency."
Would address declining enrollment "by rebuilding trust in public education."
On book challenges: the current process lets parents choose for their own children, and "I generally support that approach."
Campaign site positions: "I support keeping tax dollars in public schools" (vouchers); "I support the K-8 model" (closures); "I support expanding girls flag football."
